name: Horn of Arra'chea
summary: Across Mulgore, Arra'chea roams while Cairne Bloodhoof calls young hunters to prove their worth. The kodo's horn confirms a hunter can track prey and provide for the Shu'halo.

sections.title: A Chieftain's Test
sections.body: Passing the Rites of the Earthmother earns a youth a place atop Thunder Bluff, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof still expects his people to prove their worth. For the tauren, the hunt binds identity to lasting harmony with the land. Cairne sends young hunters to track Arra'chea, a massive, solitary kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking the bull's horn shows mastery of tracking prey across vast distances.

sections.title: Providing for the Tribe
sections.body: Bringing Arra'chea's horn to Thunder Bluff does more than display strength; it helps sustain the community. Tauren use every part of a slain beast. The trophy tells the High Chieftain where Arra'chea fell, so gathering parties can go down into the plains and harvest the kodo's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

faq.q: What is the Horn of Arra'chea?
faq.answer: The Horn of Arra'chea is taken from Arra'chea, a powerful, elusive kodo roaming Mulgore's plains. Hunters bring it to Cairne Bloodhoof as a rite of passage and proof of their tracking skill.

Arra'chea is a renowned kodo bull that circles the grasslands northeast of Thunder Bluff. His strength and wide migratory route make him a formidable quarry for hunters proving their worth to the tribe.

faq.q: Why does Cairne Bloodhoof ask for this trophy?
faq.answer: Cairne Bloodhoof asks for the trophy because he expects his people to keep proving their worth. Tracking and felling Arra'chea shows a hunter's dedication to the traditions of the Earthmother and provides resources for the community.

faq.q: What happens to the rest of the beast after it is killed?
faq.answer: Tauren use every part of the hunted animal. Once the horn confirms the kill, Cairne sends a gathering party down into Mulgore to collect the hide and meat for Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: As a tauren, presenting Arra'chea's horn to High Chieftain Cairne marks a rite of passage and proves your readiness to sustain and defend your people atop Thunder Bluff.
As a hunter, tracking Arra'chea's circular path across Mulgore tests the stalking and wilderness survival skills valued in a hunter.
